- Model consistently underestimates price spikes after bullish sentiment events, especially when supply net is negative and events are frequent.  
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves in sentiment or post-auction supply events; model lags in recognizing momentum.  
- When sentiment is bullish and supply net is negative, model fails to fully capture upward bias; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% of recent 7-day mean.  
- After a spike, model tends to overcorrect downward; apply a 1–3 day lagged mean reversion buffer to avoid premature drop.  
- If sentiment is neutral or bearish and supply net is negative, model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% of recent 14-day mean to account for hidden demand pressure.  
- For 30-day horizon, model exhibits mean reversion bias toward prior 10-day average; use 10-day moving average as baseline for correction.  
- When multiple auction events occur in a short window, model underestimates cumulative supply shock; add 1–2% adjustment for each event beyond 3.
